Method of Attack: Encrypts victim computers using DiskCryptor with a key defined by the attacker
Overwrites the disk’s master boot record (MBR), preventing access to encrypted files
Uses a plaintext configuration file (myConf.txt) storing the encryption key and shutdown time, allowing recovery if accessed before second reboot
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of $dcsys$ file in root of encrypted drives (e.g., C:\$dcsys$)
Files: C:\Users\Public\myLog.txt, C:\Users\Public\myConf.txt, C:\Users\Public\dcapi.dll, C:\Users\Public\dcinst.exe, C:\Users\Public\dccon.exe, C:\Users\Public\dcrypt.sys
Service named myCryptoraphyService running ransomware executable
Ransomware filename.exe (portable 32-bit .NET assembly combining DiskCryptor with ransom message)
